clue.text: Idiot's mind on song

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
the head is where the mind lives; 'use your head' means use your mind

explanation.surface: An insult: some fool's thoughts are wholly taken up with a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the mind word follows the song word. The 's is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is informal slang for a silly, empty-headed person, so it works as a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Twins are extremely upset and agitated

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends of something, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A parent's report: the twins are terribly upset and worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely upset' reads as one phrase meaning very distressed, but 'extremely' works only on 'are' and 'upset' acts on everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an informal idiom for being in a state of worry, anxiety or flustered excitement.

clue.text: Face banks to haggle — rejecting a quote under 55

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the column
banks are the edges of a river, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
55 in Roman numerals: L is fifty, V is five

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the letters are sent back the other way

parts.note: taken as written
to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: Bankers facing a haggle turn down a price quoted below fifty-five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is a printer's word for a typeface, not a person's face. The number 55 is a bare Roman numeral, and 'under' places the reversed piece below it in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvetica is a famous sans-serif typeface, and printers call any typeface design a face, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Alternatively set up bandsaw on the counter to make changes

indicators.note: counter means against or opposite, so the letters run in the contrary direction
read as 'in alternate fashion', it keeps every other letter and skips the rest

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on of these three words run together

explanation.surface: Workshop advice: you could put the bandsaw up on the workbench instead, to alter things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' looks like a reversal signal and 'counter' like a workbench, but 'set up' is fodder and 'on the counter' does the reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify or alter it for a new purpose, so adapts is a synonym for changes as a verb.

clue.text: Somewhere to put cigarettes and a pipe down — crack addict's heading inside

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is placed in the middle of another

parts.note: taken as written
both are ways of telling someone to be quiet
to have a crack at something is to have a try

indicators.note: a heading is what stands at the top, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A drug scene: stub out the cigarettes, put the pipe aside, the addict's head full of crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' and 'crack' paint a drugs picture, but 'pipe down' is a call for silence and 'crack' means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashtray is the dish in which smokers stub out and leave cigarettes and their ash, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Freeloaders and wife-swappers making group of women pose half-cut

indicators.note: one thing making way for another here means it is turned into the other, a swap
cut in half, a word loses its second half of letters

parts.note: swingers are couples who swap partners
the WI, Women's Institute, is a British organisation of women's clubs
the first half of this word

explanation.surface: A tabloid scene: scroungers and wife-swappers striking a drunken pose for a women's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves a word. In the swingers word, the two letters naming the women's group are replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger is someone who lives off other people's generosity without paying their way, which is what a freeloader does.

clue.text: Rattle mostly using tip of baton for beat

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rattle someone is to throw them, unsettle them; its last letter is dropped

indicators.note: a tip is the very end, here taken as the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Sir Simon Rattle, the conductor, beating time mostly with the end of his baton.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattle is capitalised to suggest the conductor, but it is the verb meaning to disconcert.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a regular pulsing rhythm, as of the heart, so the noun is a synonym for a beat.

clue.text: Old-fashioned chief turning some spies

parts.note: arch means principal or chief, as in arch-enemy

indicators.note: turning around makes the letters face back the opposite way

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies

explanation.surface: An outdated spymaster who turns some of his agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' suggests spies turned into double agents; it reverses the agency's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something belonging to an earlier period and no longer in use, which is what outdated or old-fashioned means.

clue.text: Six-footer quietly trains in a gym after work

indicators.note: after means following, setting one piece behind the other

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: letters that are worked are kneaded into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A very tall person training softly in a gym after a day at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer suggests a tall human, but here it means a creature with six feet, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is an insect, and every insect has six legs, so it is an example of a six-footed creature.

clue.text: Dish that's the opposite of T-bone

indicators.note: a compound that adds a letter, reversed in sense, takes that letter away instead

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap bone
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish which is the reverse of a T-bone steak.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-bone is read as T plus bone, so its opposite is bone minus T: the kneecap bone loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish dish of rice cooked with saffron, seafood or meat, so it is an example of a dish.

clue.text: Golfer was regularly stopping mid-swing — it helps one pack more …

indicators.note: a stopping plugs a gap, so one piece fills the middle of another
mid places the piece in the middle of the next word

parts.note: to rock is to swing to and fro

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A golfer who keeps stopping halfway through the swing, leading into a clue about packing more.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf terms dominate the surface, but the golfer gives only letters, and swing means rock. The ellipsis runs on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a frame fixed on top of a car for carrying luggage, letting a driver carry more.

clue.text: … power initially, easily approaching greens — well, one of them

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word
the first letter of this word
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Following on from the golfer, a powerful player easily reaches the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture continues: 'approaching greens' sounds like an approach shot, but greens are vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Greens are green vegetables, and a pea is one green vegetable, so the hedged phrase describes a single example.

clue.text: What gets barrister going during a trial assuming all goes well

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece falls inside another

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: what gets a word going is its very start, so the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A lawyer in court gets into stride during a hearing, if all goes well.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom 'trial' is just a test, and the barrister supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom at best means under the most favourable circumstances, the outcome when everything turns out well.

clue.text: Character from cartoon strip voiced by unknown old soldier

indicators.note: something voiced is spoken, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to strip is to bare
y is an unknown quantity in algebra
O is the abbreviation for old
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A comic-strip character voiced by an anonymous veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cartoon strip' looks like one phrase, but the definition ends at cartoon; strip is a verb to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is the picnic-basket-stealing bear from Hanna-Barbera's animated television series, a well-known cartoon character.

clue.text: Wrong to cuddle with a young man

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close in your arms, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that cuddling a young man is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: W for 'with' is a standard abbreviation, as in w/.
explanation.definitionFit: Swain is a literary word for a country youth, often a suitor or lover, so it means a young man.

clue.text: Found fantastic reduction

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters are set in an imaginary new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered an amazing price cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish or bring it into being, which is to introduce it for the first time.

clue.text: Complaint from 1 or 2

indicators.note: the answer to that clue means agitated and flustered, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the answer to 1 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical complaint coming from number one or number two, toilet talk.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 or 2' reads as the childish words for going to the toilet; really 1 across is fodder and 2 down, in a stew, is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment or illness, and this bowel disorder is an example of one.

clue.text: With no starters required, he'd put pitta back in position

indicators.note: with no starters means each word loses its first letter
putting something back here sends it in the reverse direction

parts.note: first letter and apostrophe dropped
first letter dropped
first letter dropped

explanation.surface: A diner skips the starters and puts the pitta bread back in its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' suggests a meal's first course, but means the first letters of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude is a bodily position or posture, as in ballet, as well as a stance or point of view.

clue.text: It makes things sweeter in Cheers since Norm first arrived wanting company

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so some letters go missing
first means coming before, setting these pieces at the front of the sequence

parts.note: as means since, as in 'as it rained'
par is the norm, the expected standard
ta is British slang for thanks
to have come is to have arrived
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: The sitcom Cheers, which the barfly Norm entered to a shout at every arrival, lacking customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' puts since and norm ahead of cheers. Cheers and Norm evoke the American sitcom, but they mean thanks and the standard; 'ta' is everyday British for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial low-calorie sweetener added to diet drinks, so it is something that makes food sweeter.

clue.text: Well-read boss takes Peter out

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
to peter out is to die away

explanation.surface: A cultured boss takes an employee called Peter out somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss means a raised ornament, not an employer, and 'Peter out' is the phrasal verb, its capital disguising it as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Studied can mean learned or scholarly in a subject, close in sense to the description of someone well informed through reading.

clue.text: Godless old man with new silver piercing

indicators.note: piercing goes through something, so one piece is pushed between others

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
N is the abbreviation for new
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An irreligious old man sporting a new silver piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: Old man is a slang term for father, and Ag comes from the Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan does not follow a mainstream religion, so the adjective is used loosely to mean godless or heathen.

clue.text: Shock on cutting clothes

indicators.note: something cutting into another slices into its middle

parts.note: to appal is to shock
re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: Shock at someone cutting up clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is the preposition meaning concerning, which is RE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal or trade term for garments and clothing, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Remote Portuguese city essentially bluffing

parts.note: Faro is a city in the Algarve, in southern Portugal

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone claiming a remote Portuguese city is basically a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: Faro is the gateway city for holidays on Portugal's Algarve coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far-off is a long distance away, which is what remote means when describing a place.

clue.text: Tom Hanks' character into dancing — makes sense

parts.note: Tom Hanks played Forrest Gump in the 1994 film

indicators.note: dancers whirl about the floor, so the letters whirl to fresh positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom Hanks's character getting into dancing is a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a link between the actor and the dancing, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumption is shrewd practical common sense and resourcefulness, so it means sense in that everyday meaning.

clue.text: Spinning record about a class tourist ultimately makes Pulp

indicators.note: spinning a disc turns it round, so the letters face back the other way
about means around, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only last letters are kept

parts.note: the last letter of this word
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: Spinning a record about a class tourist is what the band Pulp does.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulp is capitalised to suggest the Britpop band, whose hit Common People is about a class tourist; here it is just mush.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulp and paste are both soft, moist, shapeless masses, so the nouns work as synonyms.

clue.text: Short game between a bishop and priest on vacation

indicators.note: between sets one piece in the middle of the sequence

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A quick game played between a bishop and a priest on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short game' looks like a unit, but short is the definition and the game is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt manner is curt, and a curt reply is short, so the adjectives are synonyms in that brusque sense.

clue.text: Jack volunteers once, right

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force, renamed in 2014
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man named Jack used to volunteer, quite rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals the force no longer exists under that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack and tar are both old informal words for a sailor, as in Jack Tar, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: State tourism is affected after temperature dropped

indicators.note: things affected are altered, so the letters change their order
something dropped is let fall away, so a letter is lost

parts.note: these words lose a T
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A state's tourist trade has suffered since the temperature fell.
explanation.walkthrough: The temperature letter is removed from the fodder before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Smells grim in house occasionally

indicators.note: in means inside, so one piece sits within another
occasionally means now and then, so only some letters at intervals are kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of this word
dour means stern and grim

explanation.surface: Unpleasant smells hang about the house from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smells' reads as a verb but is the plural noun, and grim is a synonym, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents, especially unpleasant ones, so the plural noun is a synonym for smells.

clue.text: Tot wrapping present gets stuck

indicators.note: wrapping goes all round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to tot up is to add
present means here, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: A toddler trying to wrap a present gets tangled in the sticky tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot looks like a small child and present a gift; they are the verb to add and the adverb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling firmly to a surface, so adhered is the past tense matching stuck.

clue.text: Pleasant article following story

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp 10f
a fable is a story

explanation.surface: A nice piece of writing that follows a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like a placement word, but it gives a letter in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable describes someone friendly and easy to talk to, so it is a synonym for pleasant in manner.
